summary: This configuration block sets up error handling for PHP by hiding errors from users while still recording them to a log file. It only applies if the PHP 5 module is loaded on the server, and it tells PHP to track which errors occur so they can be logged for debugging purposes.

explanations.1: This checks if the Apache PHP 5 module is installed and active; everything between here and </IfModule> only runs if it is.
explanations.2: This hides PHP error messages from being displayed to website visitors—important for security so you don't leak sensitive information.
explanations.3: This tells PHP to write errors to a log file instead of just displaying them, so you have a record of what went wrong.
explanations.4: This enables error tracking, which stores details about the last error that occurred so it can be logged more completely.
explanations.5: This specifies the filename and location where PHP errors should be written—in this case, a file called 'error.log' in the web root.
